Subject: CloudMed DPA redlines + SCCs questions

Hi Aditya / Redwood team,

Attached is CloudMed's first pass redline to the DPA and a short note on SCCs/transfer language (see attachment: CloudMed_DPA_redlines_hoffman_v1.docx). A couple of points we flagged where we need Redwood confirmation before legal can proceed with the order form:

- Processor/Controller role definitions: CloudMed asks for explicit language confirming Redwood will act as "processor" and not retain any rights beyond performance of the service.
- SCCs: we prefer the latest EU Commission modular clauses; please confirm compatibility or propose alternative wording.
- Transfer impact addendum: CloudMed's data residency team requested an addendum describing fallback routing if UK/EU hosting is temporarily unavailable.
- KMS/HSM: they want to confirm whether Redwood can support customer-managed keys or provide certified HSM evidence.

Can we get an internal alignment by EOD tomorrow? If possible, suggest a short call to triage the items with our technical lead (cc'd on follow-up).

Thanks,
Maya Hoffman
Hoffman & Co. Legal (on behalf of CloudMed)

Subject: Re: CloudMed DPA redlines + SCCs questions

Hi Maya / team — good morning. I reviewed CloudMed's redline and noted a few discrete items we need to converge on. I attached a Redwood response with tracked changes (Redwood_DPA_response_trackchanges.docx). High-level comments below: 

1) Roles (processor/controller) — Acceptable to confirm Redwood as processor. Proposed clause: "Redwood acts as Processor of Personal Data on behalf of Customer, and processes Personal Data only on documented instructions from Customer..." (see doc).

2) SCCs — We can adopt the EU Commission modular clauses but need to pick the correct module set depending on the role split (Controller-Processor or Processor-Processor). Suggested path:
   - If CloudMed remains Controller and Redwood Processor, use the Controller-to-Processor SCCs (Module 2).
   - If there are joint processing elements, we should discuss role responsibilities in the SOW.

3) Transfer impact addendum / fallback routing — We support a transfer addendum that documents temporary cross-region fallback to the US in exceptional circumstances, with notice and duration caps (30-day temporary fallback). We propose a section that requires written consent from CloudMed for any fallback beyond 30 days.

4) KMS/HSM and BYOK — Clarified above; for hosted customers we provide HSM-backed keys via a managed BYOK flow for enterprise accounts. If CloudMed requires customer-controlled keys in their cloud tenancy, that would typically be part of a Private deployment SKU — we can outline the pricing impact in the order form.

5) Audit evidence — CloudMed asked for SOC 2 and encryption evidence: attached is a stub reference to our SOC 2 report and an operations evidence checklist. For procurement, we can provide timeboxed evidence delivery commitments in the order form exhibit.

Next steps:
- Aditya: confirm preferred call time with CloudMed (tomorrow 10:00am PT or 2:00pm PT).
- Ben / Aditya: confirm whether the residency fallback triggers any pricing or SLA exceptions.
- Maya / CloudMed: confirm attendee list for the call (technical lead + procurement).

Thanks — I kept comments focused and the attachment has proposed tracked language for each bullet.

Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Contracts | Redwood Inference
Attachment: Redwood_DPA_response_trackchanges.docx (proposed text, 6 pages)
